clue.text: One planning to have desserts sent back, say, at first

indicators.note: sent back tells us to read the dessert word from right to left

parts.note: tarts are desserts
say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.
at first is 1st, written with I for one as IST

explanation.surface: A diner plans to have the puddings returned to the kitchen, for instance, right at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns TARTS into STRAT; 'at first' is 1ST with the digit read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategist is a person who devises plans, especially long-term ones.

clue.text: Quiet newspaper man in small building

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
the editor, ED, is the newspaper man

explanation.surface: A hushed journalist working in a little hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed is a simple outbuilding, typically small and used for storage.

clue.text: Cord somewhat retro perhaps

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A corduroy garment described as a bit old-fashioned in style.
explanation.definitionFit: Rope is thick twisted cord, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Unfortunate tyro with grim tone describing branch of mathematics?

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hapless beginner with a stern voice tries to explain some area of maths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunate' acts on TYRO and GRIM TONE together; 'with' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Trigonometry is the part of mathematics dealing with triangles, angles and their ratios.

clue.text: Financial support for Hugh maybe

definitions.meaning: money given by a body for a purpose, such as a study award
Hugh is the first name of the English film actor surnamed ...

explanation.surface: Money being sought on behalf of someone called Hugh.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh Grant is a British actor known for romantic comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: A grant is a sum of money awarded, and Hugh Grant is the famous bearer of the surname.

clue.text: Very much legal — otherwise I may be called in?

parts.note: so as in 'so kind' means very much
licit means lawful or legal
or is used to mean otherwise, as in 'hurry or you'll miss it'

explanation.surface: A legal professional muses that, if things go otherwise, they may be summoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer: a lawyer is someone you call in when trouble arises.
explanation.definitionFit: A solicitor is the kind of lawyer one summons to deal with a legal problem.

clue.text: Dad in street quarrel

indicators.note: in places the word for dad inside the abbreviation for street

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for dad

explanation.surface: Father getting into a row out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel or brief squabble.

clue.text: In very clear manner clued "pill" in new way, easy ultimately

indicators.note: putting the letters in a new way means rearranging them
ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of cluing the word pill freshly and simply in a transparent style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in new way' rearranges CLUED PILL into PELLUCIDL; 'ultimately' takes the Y ending easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellucid means translucently clear, so the adverb describes doing something in a lucid, transparent way.

clue.text: Time man met upcoming nuisance — drama as a result!

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: in a down clue upcoming means the word met is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: When a man ran into an annoying person, a scene erupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' turns MET into TEM. The Tempest is a play by Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late play, set on an island, is a stage drama.

clue.text: Possible to understand partner of old, flexible about contact initially

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: about means the bendy word goes round the letter

parts.note: pliable means flexible

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of contact

explanation.surface: A former lover, supple about first getting in touch, can be fathomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C, from 'contact initially', inside PLIABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicable means capable of being explained and so comprehended.

clue.text: Unhappy Tory

explanation.surface: A Conservative feeling miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is feeling sad, and blue is the party colour of the British Conservatives.

clue.text: Traveller ruined goblet — despicable person!

indicators.note: ruined says the drinking cup is wrecked, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: a rotter is a cad, a despicable person

explanation.surface: A wanderer smashed a goblet, the scoundrel!
explanation.definitionFit: A globetrotter is someone who travels widely around the world.

clue.text: New court rule hit growers' work

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of the following words are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A recently imposed legal ruling has hurt farmers' business.
explanation.definitionFit: Horticulture is the art of cultivating gardens, the work of those who grow plants.

clue.text: Aims a clout — out of order, disastrous

indicators.note: out of order says the letters are not in their proper sequence and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone throws a punch, which is unacceptable behaviour and ends badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of order' in the surface means improper behaviour, but here it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamitous means causing a calamity, so ruinous or disastrous.

clue.text: These provide reading matter as reserve runs for Parliament

parts.note: to book is to reserve
in Britain a candidate stands, rather than runs, for election

explanation.surface: Kiosks that sell papers to commuters keep copies back while a candidate campaigns.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookstands are stalls or racks that display books and papers for reading.

clue.text: One defending a game point

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the gist is the main point

explanation.surface: A defender in a match argues one point of play.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologist is a person who argues in support of a doctrine or cause.

clue.text: Home schooling that seems right

definitions.note: a noun phrase sense: a sense of what seems right

parts.note: in means at home
tuition is teaching or schooling

explanation.surface: Educating children at home is the approach that feels correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition is an instinctive feeling about what is true, knowing without reasoning.

clue.text: Reactionary officer's airship

definitions.meaning: Colonel ..., a cartoon character, stands for a pompous reactionary military man

explanation.surface: A die-hard army man owns a dirigible.
explanation.walkthrough: Colonel Blimp was a British cartoon figure of the 1930s, a pompous, old-fashioned officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon colonel's name became a word for a reactionary, and it is also a non-rigid airship.

clue.text: Annoyed jacket is taken off in joint

indicators.note: the jacket is the outer layer, so the first and last letters are stripped away

parts.note: rankled means annoyed or irritated

explanation.surface: Irritated because his coat is removed at a dance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jacket is taken off' strips R and D from the ends of RANKLED.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint connecting the foot to the leg.

clue.text: Features of engines, extremely tough, dry in parts

indicators.note: extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of tough
in puts the abbreviation for dry inside the word for parts

parts.note: roles are parts in a play
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: Engine components that are very hard, with dry sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' is TT, short for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol; 'extremely' and 'in' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Throttles are valves controlling fuel flow to an engine, standard parts of one.

clue.text: Pause winter job, wife's away

indicators.note: the wife is away, meaning her letter is removed from the season word

parts.note: a mission is a task or job

explanation.surface: A man takes a break from his winter job while his wife is out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s away' removes W from WINTER, leaving INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermission is a pause, especially an interval during a performance.

clue.text: Old-fashioned uncle accepting note

indicators.note: accepting means the uncle's name takes the note inside it

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the USA
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An old-school relative accepts an IOU.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steam' as in steam radio is a British jokey usage for anything outdated.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is used informally for old-fashioned technology, as in steam radio.

clue.text: Small creature not seen before tantalises at outset

parts.note: new means not seen before

indicators.note: at the outset picks the first letter of tantalises

explanation.surface: A little animal never encountered before teases us at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt is a small amphibian, a kind of salamander.

clue.text: Celebrity's disdainful expression on way up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rats is an exclamation of disgust or disdain

explanation.surface: A famous person sneers while climbing the ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on way up' turns RATS into STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer, a celebrity.

clue.text: Admits one was needing support first of all

indicators.note: first of all takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they once relied on help.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to admit, so owns can mean concedes or acknowledges.

clue.text: Unexpectedly test desire in minor way?

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests the letters turn up in a surprising order

explanation.surface: Suddenly putting a craving to the test, but only in a small way.
explanation.definitionFit: A side street is a minor road branching off a main one.

clue.text: Band of distinction, say, describing some windows

definitions.meaning: a strip of cloth worn across the body as a mark of honour
a kind of window with sliding frames

explanation.surface: A ribbon of honour, so to speak, is used to characterise certain windows.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a ceremonial band worn over the shoulder, and sash windows have vertically sliding frames.

clue.text: A remote run upset census worker

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A distant run of results upsets someone counting the population.
explanation.definitionFit: An enumerator is an official who counts people when a census is taken.
